subject: math
title: Fractions on a Number Line
objective: Place unit fractions and equivalent fractions on a number line.

visual.title: Fraction path image
visual.caption: A number line from 0 to 1 with equal jumps for halves, thirds, and fourths.

teachingSupport.summary: Fractions on a number line are about equal spaces between 0 and 1, not just marks on the line.
teachingSupport.description: Learners start with a physical strip, move to a floor path, then draw the same equal spaces on paper before using symbols.

diagramCallouts.title: Whole interval
diagramCallouts.body: Mark 0 and 1 first so the child sees the whole before naming the parts.

diagramCallouts.title: Equal spaces
diagramCallouts.body: Count the spaces between tick marks; the denominator names the number of equal spaces.

diagramCallouts.title: Same point
diagramCallouts.body: Use 1/2 and 2/4 on the same line to show equivalent fractions visually.

helperNotes: Use tape on the floor or paper strips before asking for a written answer.
Ask the learner to point to the whole, then the equal spaces, then the target fraction.
Have the child say: I counted spaces, not tick marks.

commonMisunderstandings.mistake: Counting tick marks instead of spaces.
commonMisunderstandings.fix: Cover the tick marks and ask the learner to hop only the spaces between 0 and 1.

commonMisunderstandings.mistake: Thinking fourths are always bigger than halves because 4 is bigger than 2.
commonMisunderstandings.fix: Compare same-size strips and show that more pieces means smaller pieces.

teachingSupport.confusionPrompt: Write which part is confusing: finding the whole, making equal spaces, or placing the fraction.

funTasks: Hop the fraction path on the floor using tape marks.
Build a snack-strip model, then transfer the same spacing to a number line.
Teach a stuffed animal why 2/4 lands on the same point as 1/2.
reward: Unlock the Fraction Trail badge after a next-day recall win.

evidenceMoves.priorKnowledgeCheck: Ask learners to place 1/2 on a blank 0 to 1 line and explain what the denominator tells them before instruction starts.
evidenceMoves.misconceptionCheck: Watch for learners counting tick marks instead of spaces or treating larger denominators as larger pieces.
evidenceMoves.manipulativeRationale: Use fraction strips because they make equal spacing visible before learners move to the number line.
evidenceMoves.problemSolvingStrategy: Use the problem-solving routine: mark 0 and 1, count equal spaces, place the fraction, then compare with a second representation.
evidenceMoves.workedExample: Model why 2/4 lands at the same point as 1/2, then ask learners to critique a wrong example where 2/4 is placed after 1/2.
evidenceMoves.examplesAndNonExamples: Compare 2/4 as an equivalent example with 2/3 as a non-example for 1/2 on the same 0 to 1 line.
evidenceMoves.knowledgeConnections: Connect equal sharing, skip counting spaces, equivalent fractions, and the idea that fractions extend the number system between whole numbers.
evidenceMoves.metacognitivePrompt: Plan where the whole starts and ends, monitor whether spaces are equal, evaluate whether the answer matches the strip, and explain the strategy.
evidenceMoves.interventionTrigger: If the learner misses either quiz item or cannot explain equal spaces, assign the strip-to-line reteach and a next-day recall check.
evidenceMoves.transitionBridge: Grade 3 number-line fractions prepare learners for Grade 4 equivalent fractions, Grade 5 fraction operations, and Grade 6 ratios.
evidenceMoves.feedbackFrame: Name the accurate part of the model, identify the first spacing error, and ask for one corrected placement before scoring again.

sections.warmup: Compare halves, thirds, and fourths using equal-size visual parts.
sections.teach: Fractions show equal parts of a whole. On a number line, the denominator tells how many equal spaces fit between 0 and 1.
sections.guidedPractice: Drag 1/2, 1/3, and 3/4 to the correct tick marks.
sections.independentPractice: Solve 10 placement problems with unit fractions and equivalent fractions.
sections.activity: Build a paper strip number line and mark equal jumps.
sections.reteach: Use fraction strips first, then transfer the same spacing to the number line.
sections.challenge: Explain why 2/4 and 1/2 land on the same point.

quiz.prompt: Where does 1/2 belong on a number line from 0 to 1?
choices: At the first of three spaces
quiz.explanation: One half divides the space from 0 to 1 into two equal parts and lands in the middle.
Two fourths covers the same amount as one half.

studentFacing.mission: Rescue the fraction path by proving every jump is the same size.
studentFacing.whyItMatters: Fractions stop feeling like two random numbers when you can see them as places on a path.
studentFacing.bigIdea: The denominator tells how many equal spaces split the whole from 0 to 1.
modelSteps: Mark the whole first: 0 at the start and 1 at the end.
Split the whole into equal spaces, not just tick marks.
Place the fraction by counting spaces from 0.
studentFacing.example: For 2/4, split 0 to 1 into four equal spaces, then move two spaces. You land at the same place as 1/2.
studentFacing.nonExample: If the spaces are not equal, the point is not a fair fraction even if the label looks right.
studentFacing.quickCheck: Before you answer, point to the whole, count the equal spaces, then name the landing point.
studentFacing.studentSummary: A fraction on a number line is a location made from equal spaces.
studentFacing.tutorHandoff: Tell the tutor whether you are counting tick marks, making equal spaces, or finding the whole.

learningObjective: Place unit fractions and equivalent fractions on a number line.
successCriteria: I can mark 0 and 1 before I split the whole into equal spaces.
I can place a fraction by counting equal spaces, not just tick marks.
I can show why two equivalent fractions land on the same point.
I can explain my placement with a drawing, words, or a fraction strip.
essentialQuestion: How can a number line show that a fraction is a number and not just a piece of a shape?

knowledge: The denominator tells how many equal spaces make the whole interval from 0 to 1.
The numerator tells how many of those equal spaces to move from 0.
Equivalent fractions name the same location when their equal spaces line up.
capability: Build a fraction number line with a strip, drawing, or interactive model.
Place unit and equivalent fractions and defend the location.
reasoning: Use equal spaces and a shared whole as evidence instead of guessing from the size of the denominator.
retention: Retrieve the whole, equal spaces, and movement rule after a delay.
transfer: Use a number line to explain a fraction in a recipe, measurement, or game path.

phaseModules.title: Find the whole
phaseModules.studentAction: Point to 0 and 1 on the path, then say what the whole interval represents.
phaseModules.visualSupport: A bright floor path from 0 to 1 with a large whole marker.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can identify the whole before naming parts.

phaseModules.title: Build equal spaces
phaseModules.studentAction: Fold or split a strip into equal spaces, then copy those spaces onto the number line.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Fraction strip lined up with a number line.
phaseModules.successCheck: All spaces are the same size.

phaseModules.title: Read the fraction
phaseModules.studentAction: Use the denominator to name the number of spaces and the numerator to count the jumps.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Callouts for denominator, numerator, spaces, and jumps.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can explain both numbers without using a memorized trick.

phaseModules.title: Place and check
phaseModules.studentAction: Place halves, thirds, and fourths, then check each location against the strip.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can correct a placement using the model.

phaseModules.title: Explain the same point
phaseModules.studentAction: Compare 1/2 and 2/4 and explain why both names can point to one location.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Two fraction strips aligned to one number line point.
phaseModules.successCheck: My explanation names the shared whole and equal location.

phaseModules.title: Show your thinking
phaseModules.studentAction: Place a new fraction and explain the spaces and jumps using a drawing or sentence.

phaseModules.title: Fraction hop recall
phaseModules.studentAction: After a delay, rebuild a small 0-to-1 path and retrieve one fraction location.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can retrieve the rule without seeing the original example.

phaseModules.title: Use a measurement
phaseModules.studentAction: Use a number line to show a fraction of a meter, cup, or game path and explain the choice.
phaseModules.successCheck: The model still works when the context changes.

phaseModules.title: Choose the next move
phaseModules.studentAction: Decide whether to use a strip, draw equal spaces, retry, or explain an equivalent fraction.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can name the support that helps me learn next.

proofTasks.prompt: Place 1/3 on a 0-to-1 line after a delay.
Explain what the numerator and denominator tell you on the line.
Build and use a number line to place 3/4.
Complete a delayed Memory Vault fraction-hop check.
Use the model to show a fraction of a real measurement.

feedbackRules.result: The learner counted marks instead of spaces.
feedbackRules.hint: Cover the marks and count only the equal hops between 0 and 1.
feedbackRules.action: Route to a floor-path or fraction-strip repair.

feedbackRules.result: The learner thinks a larger denominator makes a larger piece.
feedbackRules.hint: Compare one strip split into 2 parts with the same strip split into 4 parts.
feedbackRules.action: Route to a concrete equal-parts comparison before retry.

feedbackRules.result: The learner started naming parts without identifying the whole.
feedbackRules.hint: Point to 0 and 1 first and say what distance is being divided.
feedbackRules.action: Return to orient and model phases.

reteachPaths.trigger: Placement or explanation misses the equal-space rule.
reteachPaths.action: Use a physical strip, then transfer the same folds to a number line.

prerequisiteRepairPaths.trigger: The learner cannot identify a whole or compare equal groups.
prerequisiteRepairPaths.action: Repair whole-versus-part language with sorting and matching before fractions.

challengePaths.trigger: The learner explains equivalent fractions independently.
challengePaths.action: Compare two new equivalent fractions and create a measurement example.

parentTeacherNotes: Use concrete strips, movement, drawing, and oral explanation before requiring symbols. Treat a correct placement with heavy prompting as developing evidence, not durable mastery.
accessibilityNotes: Provide a tactile strip and a spoken description of each number-line move.
Do not use color alone to distinguish numerator, denominator, or spaces.
Accept pointing, drawing, oral explanation, or keyboard interaction as evidence.
